prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a buy-to-let flat. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a flat is being used as a buy-to-let, I check the tenancy type and expected rental income early, because the deal often stands or falls on whether the rent comfortably covers our stress test and the property is let on acceptable terms."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the lease has a short unexpired term, I treat it as a key risk on a flat, because marketability and lender security can weaken quickly if the lease extension position is not clear."},{"type":"observation","content":"When service charges or ground rent look high or unpredictable, I flag them before getting too far, because the monthly surplus can disappear even if the headline rent seems strong."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I see a buy-to-let flat in a block with a managing agent, I prefer to review the building insurance and maintenance arrangements up front, because gaps there can create problems for both valuation and insurability."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the applicant is relying on projected rent rather than a signed tenancy, I want stronger evidence from the valuation and local market, because assumption-based income is less reliable for underwriting."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the flat is above or below commercial premises, I look closely at use restrictions and title wording, because mixed-use blocks can carry extra risks that do not show from the photos alone."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a buy-to-let flat has been recently refurbished, I still check the completion dates and any warranty documents, because a fresh finish does not tell me whether the fabric, electrics, or fire safety measures are sound."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the applicant already owns other rental property, I prefer to see a simple, consistent portfolio picture, because scattered or poorly documented property income makes affordability harder to rely on."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the flat is in a large block, I pay attention to any fire safety issues, cladding concerns, or remediation plans, because these can affect valuation, lending appetite, and future resale."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a remortgage request on a buy-to-let flat comes in with no change in tenancy or ownership, I still re-check the basics, because small changes in rent, costs, or lease terms can alter the case enough to change the decision."}]}
